es: Reconocer el lenguaje de los titulares y el sesgo o énfasis que introducen sus palabras con carga.

teaching.en: The headline says crisis, but the article only mentions a short delay.
teaching.es: El titular dice crisis, pero el artículo solo menciona un retraso corto.
teaching.explanationEs: Una palabra fuerte (crisis) puede dramatizar un hecho pequeño: compáralo con el artículo.
segments: The headline says crisis, but the
article only mentions a short delay.
teaching.audioText: The headline says crisis, but the article only mentions a short delay.

teaching.en: A good hook makes you click, but it can exaggerate a small problem.
teaching.es: Un buen gancho hace que hagas clic, pero puede exagerar un problema pequeño.
teaching.explanationEs: Hook es lo que atrapa al lector; exaggerate es mostrar algo más grande de lo que es.
segments: A good hook makes you click, but
it can exaggerate a small problem.
teaching.audioText: A good hook makes you click, but it can exaggerate a small problem.

teaching.en: Shock as bus fares rise again.
teaching.es: Impacto: los billetes de autobús suben otra vez.

segments: Shock as bus
fares rise again.
teaching.audioText: Shock as bus fares rise again.

teaching.en: The calm headline says the library will close on Mondays; the loaded one says readers are being punished.
teaching.es: El titular sereno dice que la biblioteca cerrará los lunes; el cargado dice que los lectores están siendo castigados.
teaching.explanationEs: Loaded = con carga emocional; el mismo hecho se cuenta con tono distinto.
segments: The calm headline says the library will close on
Mondays; the loaded one says readers are being punished.
teaching.audioText: The calm headline says the library will close on Mondays; the loaded one says readers are being punished.

teaching.en: A misleading headline shows its bias with words that tell you how to feel.
teaching.es: Un titular engañoso muestra su sesgo con palabras que te dicen cómo sentirte.
teaching.explanationEs: Bias es la inclinación a un lado; se nota en las palabras elegidas.
segments: A misleading headline shows its bias with
words that tell you how to feel.
teaching.audioText: A misleading headline shows its bias with words that tell you how to feel.

teaching.en: The strongest word gets the emphasis, so readers notice it before the facts.
teaching.es: La palabra más fuerte recibe el énfasis, así que los lectores la notan antes que los hechos.
teaching.explanationEs: Emphasis = lo que se destaca; en un titular suele ir al principio.
segments: The strongest word gets the emphasis, so
readers notice it before the facts.
teaching.audioText: The strongest word gets the emphasis, so readers notice it before the facts.

Crisis at library as Monday hours change
Library changes opening hours on Mondays

es: Usar accuse of, deny, admit, claim to have e insist on con su patrón para reportar lo que dicen otras personas en una noticia.

teaching.en: The neighbours accused the company of dumping waste in the river.
teaching.es: Los vecinos acusaron a la empresa de verter residuos en el río.
teaching.explanationEs: Accuse + persona + of + verbo en -ing; no se dice «accused to dump».
segments: The neighbours accused the company of
dumping waste in the river.
teaching.audioText: The neighbours accused the company of dumping waste in the river.

teaching.en: The spokesperson denied dumping anything and said the photos were old.
teaching.es: El portavoz negó haber vertido nada y dijo que las fotos eran antiguas.
teaching.explanationEs: Deny va seguido de un verbo en -ing: denied dumping.
segments: The spokesperson denied dumping anything and
said the photos were old.
teaching.audioText: The spokesperson denied dumping anything and said the photos were old.

teaching.en: The manager admitted leaving a gate open, but he insisted on paying for the clean-up.
teaching.es: El gerente admitió haber dejado una puerta abierta, pero insistió en pagar la limpieza.
teaching.explanationEs: Admitted + -ing reconoce un hecho; insisted on + -ing muestra firmeza.
segments: The manager admitted leaving a gate open, but
he insisted on paying for the clean-up.
teaching.audioText: The manager admitted leaving a gate open, but he insisted on paying for the clean-up.

teaching.en: The company claimed to have checked the river every week.
teaching.es: La empresa aseguró haber revisado el río cada semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim to have + participio: afirma algo ya hecho sin garantizar que sea verdad.
segments: The company claimed to have
checked the river every week.
teaching.audioText: The company claimed to have checked the river every week.

teaching.en: Its statement does not say who is responsible.
teaching.es: Su comunicado no dice quién es el responsable.
teaching.explanationEs: El comunicado es el texto oficial de la empresa; responsible = con la responsabilidad.
segments: Its statement does not
say who is responsible.
teaching.audioText: Its statement does not say who is responsible.

prompt.es: Tom dijo: «Leo rompió la ventana». ¿Cómo lo reporta?

choices.text: Tom accused Leo to break the window.
Tom accused Leo for breaking the window.
Tom accused Leo of breaking the window.

feedback.es: Con accuse se usa persona + of + -ing: accused Leo of breaking.

hint.es: Después de accused y la persona va of, y el verbo termina en -ing.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia negó haber perdido las llaves.»

feedback.es: Deny se construye con -ing: denied losing (o having lost para marcar que fue antes).

hint.es: Después de deny va un verbo terminado en -ing.

answer.text: The coach insisted on paying for the bus

feedback.es: Insist se une a on y a un verbo en -ing: insisted on paying.

hint.es: Insisted va seguido de on y de un verbo en -ing.

prompt.es: Completa tres noticias con el patrón correcto.

feedback.es: Accuse lleva of + -ing, claim lleva to have + participio y deny se construye con -ing.

sentences: The teacher accused two students ___ copying the test.
The club claimed ___ have sold every ticket.

prompt.es: Reporta lo que dijo Ana usando el verbo denied.

accepted: Ana denied having taken the bike.
Ana denied that she took the bike.

feedback.es: Denied + -ing reporta una negación: denied taking the bike.

origin.text: Ana dijo: «I did not take the bike.» Escribe una frase que reporte su negación.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dice la portavoz sobre los exámenes.

choices.text: That she had not read the papers early and had locked them away.
That she read the papers early and was very sorry.
That the teacher had taken the papers home.

feedback.es: La portavoz negó haber leído los exámenes antes de tiempo y aseguró haberlos guardado bajo llave.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo se reporta correctamente lo que dijo Leo?

choices.text: Leo denied to open the box.
Leo denied opening the box.
Leo insisted on opening the box.

feedback.es: Leo niega haber abierto la caja, y deny va con -ing; insisted on expresa firmeza y denied to open no es el patrón.

origin.text: Leo: «I did not open the box.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los vecinos acusaron al club de hacer demasiado ruido.»

answer.text: The neighbours accused the club of making too much noise

feedback.es: La acusación se construye con accused + persona + of + -ing: accused the club of making.

prompt.es: Completa: «El jefe admitió haber cometido un error.»

feedback.es: Admitted + -ing reconoce un hecho incómodo, en este caso un error.

origin.text: The boss ___ making a mistake.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué acusan los fans al grupo.

choices.text: Of singing badly.
Of raising the price of tickets.
Of cancelling shows too often.

feedback.es: Los fans acusan al grupo de cancelar demasiados conciertos: accused + of + -ing.

prompt.es: ¿Qué verbo usa un periodista que duda de lo que dice el alcalde?

choices.text: claimed
admitted
insisted

origin.text: The mayor ___ to have read the whole report.

feedback.es: Negar una acción pasada se reporta con denied + -ing.

Ana
Nobody

es: Separar hechos verificables, opiniones e insinuaciones en noticias y publicaciones, fijándose en las palabras que empujan al lector.

teaching.en: According to the survey, sixty per cent of residents use the library every week.
teaching.es: Según la encuesta, el sesenta por ciento de los residentes usa la biblioteca cada semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Según una fuente + una cifra: se trata de un dato que se puede comprobar.
segments: According to the survey, sixty per cent
of residents use the library every week.
teaching.audioText: According to the survey, sixty per cent of residents use the library every week.

teaching.en: The new timetable is obviously a terrible idea.
teaching.es: El nuevo horario es obviamente una idea terrible.
teaching.explanationEs: Obviously y terrible no describen un dato: expresan un juicio personal.
segments: The new timetable is
obviously a terrible idea.
teaching.audioText: The new timetable is obviously a terrible idea.

teaching.en: The figure of two hundred complaints is a fact: you can verify it in the council records.
teaching.es: La cifra de doscientas quejas es un hecho: puedes comprobarla en los registros del ayuntamiento.
teaching.explanationEs: Un fact se puede verificar con registros, fechas o cifras.
segments: The figure of two hundred complaints is a fact:
you can verify it in the council records.
teaching.audioText: The figure of two hundred complaints is a fact: you can verify it in the council records.

segments: The report does not say the mayor lied,
but the headline seems to imply it.
teaching.audioText: The report does not say the mayor lied, but the headline seems to imply it.

teaching.en: Without evidence, a claim is only an opinion.

segments: Without evidence, a claim
is only an opinion.
teaching.audioText: Without evidence, a claim is only an opinion.

The library is the best place in town.

es: Resumir una noticia atribuyendo cada afirmación a su fuente, marcando lo no confirmado y reportando una pregunta ajena.

teaching.en: According to an official, the market will open again on Saturday.
teaching.es: Según un funcionario, el mercado volverá a abrir el sábado.

segments: According to an official, the market
will open again on Saturday.
teaching.audioText: According to an official, the market will open again on Saturday.

teaching.en: A witness said that the water reached half a metre in the square.

segments: A witness said that the water reached

teaching.audioText: A witness said that the water reached half a metre in the square.

segments: The cause is reportedly a broken

segments: The mayor's office has not been

segments: A good summary gives a source for every
